summary: Backend testing of the NEW alternative-2FA methods (email OTP + trusted-device 30-day bypass) added on top of the existing TOTP flow. Created /app/backend/tests/test_admin_2fa_alt_methods.py with 18 focused pytest cases across 8 test classes and got 18/18 PASS on first execution against the public URL (43.6s). Coverage matches the review checklist exactly: login response now returns availableMethods={'totp','email'} and obfuscated emailHint; GET /api/admin/2fa/methods returns methods+emailHint+hasBackupCodes with the challenge Bearer; POST /api/admin/2fa/email/send sends via Gmail SMTP (verified 200 + obfuscated sentTo + expiresInMinutes=10 + resendAfterSeconds=30 + row present in admin_email_otps with code_hash + attempts=0); a second /email/send within 30s returns 429 with 'wait Ns' detail; email-OTP success path verified end-to-end by directly injecting a KNOWN bcrypt-hashed code row into admin_email_otps and calling /api/admin/2fa/login with method='email' (returns full JWT that works on /admin/me and burns the row); 5 wrong email codes each return 401 and the 6th attempt with the CORRECT code still returns 401 because the row is deleted after the 5th failure; method='totp' works; method='totp'+trustDevice=true returns trustDeviceToken + trustDeviceDays=30; subsequent /api/admin/login with X-Admin-Trust-Token header returns status='ok', trustedDevice=true, no needs_2fa; GET /api/admin/trusted-devices lists id,userAgent,createdAt,lastUsedAt,expiresAt; DELETE /api/admin/trusted-devices/{id} removes just that device and re-login with the same trust token now correctly returns needs_2fa; DELETE /api/admin/trusted-devices (all) returns {ok, revoked:N} with N matching prior count and empty list afterwards; auto-detect fallback preserved (both TOTP and backup codes without a `method` field still work; explicit method='backup' still works); /api/admin/2fa/disable with valid TOTP purges admin_trusted_devices AND admin_email_otps for that admin (verified via direct Mongo counts); /api/admin/2fa/reset/{admin_id} by super admin also purges trusted devices + email OTPs on the target admin; backup-codes/regenerate still returns 10 new codes. Teardown verified: master admin ends with twoFactorEnabled=null, no trusted devices, no email OTP rows, no test_* admins left over — user's own login is unblocked.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: _consume_email_otp is called for BOTH method='email' AND the auto-detect fallback branch. If a challenger picks method='totp' but happens to type 6 digits that match a stale email OTP row's hash, no cross-pollination happens (good) — but note that auto-detect calls _consume_email_otp AFTER a failed TOTP check, which increments the email-OTP attempts counter even when the user was actually trying a TOTP. Not a security issue but a UX quirk: a legitimate user mis-typing their TOTP 5 times will silently burn their pending email OTP. Consider only calling _consume_email_otp in auto-detect if there IS a pending email OTP row for that admin (i.e., short-circuit when db.admin_email_otps.find_one is None).

server.py L866-873: rate-limit block uses datetime.fromisoformat(prev['sent_at']) inside a broad try/except that silently swallows non-HTTPException errors. A corrupt/missing sent_at will bypass the 30s throttle. Consider defaulting to 0s remaining explicitly when parsing fails.

server.py L299: userAgent is stored truncated to [:255] but never HTML-escaped. The list endpoint returns it raw — if the trusted-devices UI ever renders it without escaping, this is an XSS vector (admin-controlled but still). Minor.

server.py L308 _check_trusted_device: on successful use, `lastUsedAt` is bumped but `expiresAt` is NOT slid forward — trust tokens are hard-30-days from creation, not from last use. That matches the review request (30 days) but consider documenting so users don't expect rolling renewal.
server.py has grown to 2574 lines (up from 2287 last iteration). Splitting into admin.py, admin_2fa.py, admin_trusted_devices.py etc. is overdue.

The /api/admin/2fa/methods response includes hasBackupCodes but the availableMethods list never includes 'backup'. If frontend consistency is desired, either include 'backup' in availableMethods or rename to something like `primaryMethods`. Not a bug — just an interface-vocabulary observation.

success_rate.backend: 100% (18/18 pytests passed on first run in 43.6s against public URL)

test_credentials: Master admin username=master password=1121211221. During testing 2FA was enabled on master via the /api/admin/2fa/setup + /enable flow; teardown fully disables 2FA on master and clears admin_trusted_devices + admin_email_otps so the user's own login is not blocked. Verified post-test Mongo state: twoFactorEnabled=None, trusted devices count=0, email OTP count=0, no residual test_* admins.
seed_data_creation: Temporary admins with usernames matching ^test_ were created and deleted by the test's autouse fixture teardown (_cleanup_test_admins). Direct Mongo writes were used to (a) inject a KNOWN bcrypt-hashed email OTP row so the success path could be verified without reading an inbox, and (b) inject a fake email OTP row on a target admin to verify /api/admin/2fa/reset purges it. No production data was touched. Post-test verification: 0 orphan rows in either admin_trusted_devices or admin_email_otps.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Regression file for this feature is /app/backend/tests/test_admin_2fa_alt_methods.py — safe to re-run any time; it enrolls, tests, then wipes 2FA and all trust/otp rows on master via module-scoped autouse fixture. Runtime ~44s. Tests use several 1-sec sleeps between rapid TOTP generations to avoid replay collisions inside the same 30s TOTP window; if you compress them, you'll get sporadic 401s. The email-OTP-success test intentionally bypasses SMTP by writing a KNOWN bcrypt hash directly to admin_email_otps and calling /api/admin/2fa/login with method='email' — this is the pragmatic pattern documented in the review request. If a future run needs to test the FULL end-to-end email path with a real inbox, integrate an SMTP capture (e.g. mailhog) but note this test suite doesn't require it. If code changes touch /api/admin/2fa/login auto-detect logic, keep in mind the current order is TOTP → email OTP → backup code and that the email OTP branch increments attempts even on TOTP misses (see critical_code_review_comments).
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — this iteration is a green-field feature test, not a bug fix. All 18 checks passed on first execution.
